analysis.title: "Growth Shock": When The AI Trade Sneezes, Bonds Now Rally, And BofA Has A Hedge For It
key_insights: BofA's Global Equity Volatility Insights note says AI-driven weakness now trades as a growth shock. On Oct 22 the 10-year yield fell more than 16bps while the Nasdaq fell nearly 3%.

Earlier in the year AI scares came with higher yields. BofA now sees stocks and yields falling together in an AI unwind, which matches the market reaction to the OpenAI revenue scare two weeks earlier.

The implied vol spread between Nasdaq and S&P (VXN minus VIX) is back near 9-10 vol points, and the realised spread has also widened. BofA reads this as the Nasdaq reacting more than the S&P to AI news.
BofA keeps its preference for owning Nasdaq over S&P in both delta and vol as the AI bubble keeps building.

Bear hedge: an NDX September 2027 90% max lookback put that pays only if 10-year SOFR swap rates fall at least 25bps. The strike resets to 90% of the highest daily NDX close, so the buyer does not need to time the top.

The hybrid was first pitched on Oct 12 at 3.62% indicative cost, a 46% discount to the plain max lookback put and 23bps cheaper than a vanilla put. Rates have drifted lower and demand has pushed the correlation entry point higher, so it is less cheap now.

BofA still likes the hybrid because rates are unlikely to fall as far as in a prolonged AI unwind, and its outright cost remains attractive against other longer-dated hedges. NDX expanding put spreads contingent on lower rates are a cheaper, capped alternative.
Bull trade: megacap earnings, the October FOMC and the midterm elections could together act as a clearing event for risk into year-end and spark a bullish sentiment shift.

For investors who cut risk, BofA recommends call spreads. Among options-liquid ETFs that sold off since the Oct 6 Nasdaq peak, SMH and EEM offer the best payout ratios on December ATM / +1-sigma call spreads at about 2.8x, and SPY is lowest at about 2x.
Among Nasdaq 100 single names that sold off since the peak, TMUS and WDC lead with payouts near 4x on the same call spreads. SPCX, LITE, CEG and LRCX follow.
BofA concedes the absolute payout ratios may appear modest. Moving the lower strike further out-of-the-money would raise the potential payoff.

The article's author (ZeroHedge, not BofA) leans toward the growth shock outcome. They cite the OpenAI revenue miss, CoreWeave's selloff and the Oct 22 drop, each with bonds rallying, and say the open question is who pays for the AI buildout and at what return.

tension_points.bull_case: Megacap earnings, the October FOMC and the midterms could act as a clearing event for risk into year-end and spark a bullish sentiment shift. BofA suggests call spreads on SMH, EEM and sold-off Nasdaq 100 names.
tension_points.bear_case: AI-driven weakness trades as a growth shock, with yields falling as the Nasdaq falls (Oct 22: 10-year yield down more than 16bps, Nasdaq down nearly 3%). BofA offers a contingent NDX lookback put for a long AI unwind.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If the megacap earnings, the October FOMC and the midterms pass without another AI-led selloff, BofA expects a clearing event and a bullish sentiment shift.
